description: Line solving finds every cell value of one nonogram row or column that some placement of its runs allows. A forward pass marks the states (cell `i`, runs placed `j`) that the line can reach from its start under the current domains, and a backward pass marks the states from which the rest of the line still fits. A cell keeps the value *empty* or *filled* only if a move between a reachable state and a completable state uses it; values other than 0 and 1 are removed. The result is complete for the line and costs `O(n · k · L)` for `n` cells, `k` runs and the longest run `L`. Use one per row and column under propagation, which carries each deduction to the crossing lines.

papers.authors: K. J. Batenburg, W. A. Kosters
papers.title: Solving Nonograms by combining relaxations
